subject: CloudCraft integration - solution compatibility audit and validation
messages:
From: Samira Khan <samira@cloudcraft.io>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: partners@cloudcraft.io
Date: 2026-03-25T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: CloudCraft x Redwood - request for solution compatibility audit

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for taking this call last week. CloudCraft is moving forward with a proof-of-concept embedding Redwood into our partner toolkit for in-app search and assistant workflows. Before we allocate engineering time for an in-depth integration, we need a short technical compatibility audit and a reference-design review to confirm there are no blockers around networking, KV cache behavior, and quantized variants.

Attached: CloudCraft_integration_checklist.xlsx (checklist + sample traffic profile).

Questions we want covered in the audit:
- Minimum desired latency SLOs and how Redwood handles cold-starts for small bursts
- Any special firewall/VPC setup needed for private deployment or dedicated pools
- Recommendations for model variants (fp16 vs int8) given our 2–3k token average response size

Can we aim for a short review document and a set of validation test cases by the end of next week? Also happy to run a short working session with your architects.

Thanks,
Samira
Partner Lead, CloudCraft

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira@cloudcraft.io>
Cc: stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com, jonas.weber@redwood.com, grace.oconnor@redwood.com
Date: 2026-03-25T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: CloudCraft x Redwood - request for solution compatibility audit

Samira —

Appreciate the checklist and the traffic profile. We're glad to help and can turn this into a focused "compatibility audit" + validation plan. High-level approach I propose:

1) Reference design review (we'll produce a one-page reference design and a PDF appendix showing network flows and model variant recommendations) — attachment: redwood-reference-design-v0.9.pdf
2) Pre-validation checklist (runbook for network and credentials, which we'll share as a lightweight MD file)
3) Integration smoke tests (throughput and latency tests against a staging endpoint and a set of deterministic prompts)
4) Security/compliance pre-check (brief list of evidentiary items we may need for Dedicated/Private paths)

Two quick asks to scope this properly:
- Can you share a sanitized sample payload distribution (tokens per request, concurrency expectations) — the XLS helped but a sample trace is ideal
- Are you planning Hosted API first, or do you expect a Dedicated/private deployment in the PoC? That changes our network checklist and the signing/credential flow.

I propose we run an architecture working session on Thu 2026-03-28 10:00 PT — 45 minutes to walk the reference design and agree on the validation matrix. If that works, I'll send a calendar invite and a short pre-read.

Marissa Cole
Head of Partner Integrations, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0132

---
Attachment: redwood-reference-design-v0.9.pdf (reference design + model selection guidance)

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, jonas.weber@redwood.com, grace.oconnor@redwood.com
Date: 2026-03-26T11:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: CloudCraft x Redwood - request for solution compatibility audit

Marissa / team —

Adding a few security/compliance items we'll want surfaced in the pre-read so CloudCraft can decide Hosted vs Dedicated for the PoC: 

- SOC 2 / evidence: list of logs we can provide (audit logs, token usage, admin actions) — we should include the sample retention policy in the pre-read
- Network setup: if they want Dedicated / Private, VPC peering or PrivateLink? We need their CIDR blocks and egress rules.
- Data residency: confirm whether PII will be passed in prompts; if so, we recommend a Private deployment for the test window
- Credentials flow: OAuth vs API key + short-lived tokens for staging; document the recommended vault integration (KMS/HSM notes)

I'll draft a short integration_testplan.md and attach it to the shared Drive. Also: we should request a small set of acceptance prompts (sanitized) that exercise long context and retrieval-heavy queries — that will guide the model variant choice.

-Stephanie
Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
---
Attachment: redwood-integration_testplan.md (stub, will populate with test cases and acceptance criteria)

From: Samira Khan <samira@cloudcraft.io>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Ethan Blake <ethan.blake@cloudcraft.io>, partners@cloudcraft.io
Date: 2026-03-30T15:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: CloudCraft x Redwood - request for solution compatibility audit

Hi Marissa / team —

This plan looks good — thanks for the quick turnaround. Confirming the following:

- We will start with Hosted API for the PoC, and if latency or data policy requires it we will target Dedicated in phase 2.
- I'll upload a small set of sanitized sample prompts and a 24-hour trace to the Drive link you shared.
- Our staging environment (staging.cloudcraft.io) will be ready for Redwood to run the smoke tests on 2026-04-02.

Links: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2bCk-cloudcraft-integration (uploaded: sample-trace.json, network_diagram.png)
Jira: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INTG-412 (we created a ticket and linked engineering EPIC)

Let's lock the Thu 03/28 10:00 PT working session; Ethan will join from our infra team and can walk the staging networking. After the meeting we expect Redwood to deliver the one-page reference design and a short validation matrix by EOW (2026-04-02).

Samira
Partner Lead, CloudCraft
---
Attachment stubs: network_diagram.png, sample-trace.json
